    Tiny penny-farthings: an almost projective-injective point #

    A variant of not_minimal_of_projInj used for the open penny-farthing case of [mild] Theorem 3 (replacing the Auslander–Reiten argument of [Standard] §3.1, §3.2). Let e, e' be idempotents, s ∈ e' B e nonzero, and t ∈ e_b B e with R t = 0, e' B t = 0, such that

    • the elements of B e whose R-multiples lie in k t lie in k s + k t;
    • the elements of e' B killed by R on the right lie in k s;
    • every element of e_b R is a left multiple t b', and e_b is local.

    Then for a module U with s u ≠ 0 the map B e → U, b ↦ b u, composed with U → (e'B)^*, m ↦ (c ↦ ψ(c m)), is surjective with kernel inside k t, and an indecomposable U not killed by s is B e or B e / (t): if t u = 0, B e / (t) splits off; if t u lies in R V (V the kernel of U → (e'B)^*) one changes u so that t u = 0; otherwise B e splits off modulo a complement of k t u in V. Hence B is not minimal representation-infinite. For t = 0 this is the projective-injective case.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.nonempty_equiv_of_retract {B : Type u} [Ring B] {M U : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup U] [Module B U] (hU : Statement.IsIndecomposable B U) (F : M →ₗ[B] U) (hF : F ≠ 0) (W : Submodule B U) (hbij : Function.Bijective ⇑(W.mkQ ∘ₗ F)) :
    Nonempty (U ≃ₗ[B] M)

    A module map F : M → U that becomes bijective modulo a submodule W of an indecomposable U is an isomorphism onto U (it splits, r = (q F)⁻¹ q).
